data.name: Mokshika
data.gender_notes: Mokshika is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Mokshika is a Sanskrit name derived from the root words 'moksha' (liberation) and 'ika' (one). It symbolizes the quest for spiritual enlightenment and liberation from the cycle of birth and death. The name is associated with the goddess Laxmi, who is believed to grant moksha (salvation) to her devotees. The name Mokshika carries the meaning “Liberation from suffering” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Mokshika usually hope their child will grow to embody liberation from suffering and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of liberation and spiritual growth
data.etymology: Mokshika belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Liberation from suffering.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mokshika total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

historical_references.reference: Mokshika was an influential woman in the court of Emperor Akbar, who ruled India from 1556 to 1605. She was renowned for her wisdom and knowledge of the Hindu scriptures, particularly the Vedas and the Upanishads. Mokshika's influence extended beyond the palace, and she played a significant role in spreading and promoting Hinduism in India during Akbar's reign.

Mokshika was a revered female sage mentioned in Hindu mythology, often identified with the goddess Saraswati, the goddess of knowledge and wisdom. She is believed to have lived during the Treta Yuga, around the time of the epic Ramayana. Mokshika is often depicted as a beautiful woman with a veena (a stringed musical instrument) and a cup of knowledge (jhara) in her hands.
